forecasts.reason: The freeze saves about 0.86 s at 231 steps and the extra 0.5 epoch costs about 0.3 s, so time ≤5.75 is near-certain. The +0.2 pp from the epochs roughly cancels the freeze's −0.2 pp, which leaves a held-out mean ≥0.754 at about a coin flip.

uint8→GPU already happens in prepare. Only trial 0's first-call warm-up (eigh, unfold) remains, about 0.05 s on the 3-trial mean, which sits right at the threshold. Bit-identity is likely but not guaranteed (cuDNN).

The bias already stops learning at about 34%, so the gain is only the dgrad of conv1 and GELU backward on 31×31 maps (24 channels) for about 80% of steps. The bandwidth-bound stem pushes the saving to about 2%, at the threshold. The trajectory re-rolls.

Freezing 15% more of the steps (part at 28 px) saves another 0.35–0.45 s. But E028 already lost about 0.2 pp at 25% frozen, and doubling the frozen share likely loses ≥0.25 pp, outside the 0.15 pp limit.

With no recipe change the metrics repeat the tip. E029/E030/E032 on the same stream suggest a population mean of about 0.7525, so the pooled 20-seed mean is more likely below 0.753 (winner's curse on seeds 3–12).

Assumed to run on the I052 recipe. Removing the BN stat reductions on 31×31 maps in a forward-only frozen phase saves about 0.05–0.1 s, near the 2% threshold. Eval-mode BN slightly shifts the inputs to group 2, a small accuracy risk.
E028's ~45% per-step saving for ~20% of MACs implies non-GEMM traffic on the large maps dominates the stem. A profile should show ≥30% non-GEMM time and a group-1 plus whitening share ≥35%.
Dropping the Muon Newton-Schulz step saves about 3%. Muon's real gain is likely about 0.4 pp of E006's 0.66, so held-out loses ≥0.3 pp, as the hypothesis predicts.

cruxes: Does E028's 0.84 s freeze saving (~45% of a 32 px step for ~20% of MACs) reproduce on the E027 base? If so, freeze plus extra epochs is the only lever with a rate clearly above 2 s/pp, and I052 should be kept even at a small held-out accuracy cost.

What is the tip's true population mean: about 0.7525 (as E029/E030/E032 imply) or about 0.754 (seeds 3–12)? This decides whether every next time cut must first buy accuracy back, and whether the 40-seed bar is already at risk.

Is the frozen-phase stem cost mostly BN/GELU memory traffic, or conv dgrad/wgrad? That sets whether I057 and I054 are worth ≥2% each, or whether only moving the freeze point (which costs accuracy) still pays.
structured_output.world_model: W3 (cost lens), after E032. Tip E027: 5.878 s, 0.7547 on seeds 0–2. Its population mean is about 0.7525, because E029/E030/E032 on the same stream all fell. Time ≈ 0.5 s fixed + pixel-weighted steps; a 32 px step costs about 0.032 s, and a frozen-stem 32 px step saves about 0.015 s (E028), so the large-map stem is bandwidth-bound. Code facts: uint8→GPU is already done in prepare; the whitening bias lr goes to 0 at 34% of steps but its gradient is still computed; filters are renormalized, so filter wd does nothing. Rates: epochs 1.5–2.5 s/pp; freeze about 4 s/pp at a 25% dose, with diminishing returns as the dose grows. Every schedule booster tested (LS, the two-stage LS of E032, warm-up, Lookahead interval, alpha exponent) was flat or negative. The plan is to bank freeze savings and spend part of them on epochs (I052), and to treat further stem levers (I054, I057) as roughly 2% each.
